article_content: LONDON, England (CNN) -- The 2002 World Cup was the first tournament held in Asia, bringing the world's attention to the continent's footballing talents. Michael Chopra was the first player of Indian parentage to play and score in the English Premier League. The event was Asia's chance to showcase its footballing prowess, with South Korea reaching the semi-finals. However, few footballers of Asian origin have made an impact outside the Asian Federation Cup (AFC) since then. A new initiative by Chelsea FC aims to find talented youngsters from Asian backgrounds. Chelsea has partnered with the Football Association (FA), Kick It Out, and the Asian Media Group for 'The Search for an Asian Star' event in May at Stamford Bridge, London. The search is open to players under 12, 13, and 14 from London and south-east England with Indian, Pakistani, Sri Lankan, or Bangladeshi backgrounds. 'We hope this competition inspires Asian youngsters,' said Graeme Le Saux, former Chelsea and England full-back.

article_content: Australians attending next year's Gallipoli centenary Anzac Day commemorations have been warned by the government to be vigilant due to increased terrorism threats. The Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade has released preliminary advice on the risk facing travellers heading to Turkey for the event on the Gallipoli Peninsula in April. While there's currently no indication that terrorist groups intend to attack Australians in Turkey, the department warns people should 'exercise a high degree of caution'. Foreign Minister Julie Bishop has voiced her fears over a possible terrorist attack. Bishop stated that Turkey was on the front line of the ongoing wars in Iraq and Syria, and that 'the security environment is volatile.' The Department of Veterans' Affairs said that a spill-over from the Syrian conflict could lead to attacks against targets in Turkey. Turkish authorities will screen all visitors on arrival, and all bags will be searched and prohibited items confiscated.

article_content: Swiss authorities are continuing their search for 6-year-old twins Alessia and Livia Schepp, abducted by their father, Matthias Schepp, over a week ago. The investigation now spans three countries: Switzerland, France, and Italy, following Matthias Schepp's death in Bari, Italy. The 43-year-old father took his own life on a railway in Cerignola, Italy, about 60 miles west of Bari. Police discovered that Schepp had bought ferry tickets for himself and the girls to travel from Marseilles to Corsica, but it's unclear if they boarded. The twins were last seen on January 30 when their father took them from their St. Sulpice home near Lausanne, Switzerland. The girls are described as being about 3 feet, 9 inches tall with blond hair; Livia wore a green T-shirt, jeans, a violet ski jacket, and Adidas sneakers, while Alessia wore a red and white striped T-shirt, jeans, a brown jacket, and black shoes. Interpol issued a Yellow Notice for the missing girls, prompting a widespread search effort called 'Operation Gemelle'.

article_content: Crisis begets innovation. During the Great Depression, Americans and Britons developed key technologies like television and refrigeration. Today, three areas show promise: the transition from coal to natural gas, downtown revival, and advancements in mental health. The shift to natural gas, which emits half as much carbon dioxide as coal, could drive economic activity and a more sustainable future. Americans are moving to downtown areas, seen in cities like Cleveland and Detroit, potentially reducing commuting times and changing how we use space. Twenty years after Prozac's advent, understanding of depression has grown. Further progress could lead to new industries and reduce mental illness's economic burden.

article_content: Arturo Gatti, an Italian-born Canadian boxer, is remembered for his thrilling fights with Micky 'Irish' Ward. Gatti's professional boxing career lasted 16 years, during which he secured world titles at super featherweight and junior welterweight. The bouts between Gatti and Ward in 2002 and 2003 are particularly notable; two of these fights won the 'Fight of the Year' award from Ring Magazine. In their third encounter, Gatti continued fighting despite breaking his right hand, ultimately winning by unanimous decision. Although Gatti achieved later successes, including becoming the WBC junior welterweight champion, his contests against Ward remain the pinnacle of his career. Gatti's personal life was marked by controversy, including an assault charge related to his then-girlfriend, Amanda Rodriguez, whom he subsequently married. Gatti concluded his career with a record of 49 fights, comprising 31 knockouts and nine defeats.

article_content: Most of us have agreed to share a cab with a stranger while traveling, but we haven't wound up in jail as a result. That 'wrong-place-wrong-time' nightmare scenario is what's apparently happened to Stacey Addison, an American veterinarian from Oregon, who has been traveling solo around the world since January 2013. According to the Oregonian newspaper and Addison's Facebook page, on September 5, Addison traveled from Indonesia into Timor-Leste and shared a cab from the border crossing at Batugade to the capital city of Dili. 'Along the way, another passenger asked to pick up a package at a DHL office,' reports the Oregonian. 'Police, acting on a tip from Indonesian authorities, were watching and found methamphetamine in the parcel.' Addison and everyone else in the cab were arrested. 'I was held in the Dili Detention Center for four nights then released after an initial hearing,' Addison later posted on Facebook. 'The judge ordered that my passport be held until further investigations have been completed.' Addison was conditionally released on September 9 but wasn't allowed to leave the country. Prosecutors told her she was needed as a witness for an investigation that could take a year. After an October 29 court appearance, Addison was jailed again without explanation or warning and spent five days in solitary confinement. It's unclear when Addison will be released. The Oregonian reports that local U.S. consular officials have visited Addison in prison twice, and U.S. State Department officials will meet with the Timorese ambassador. Addison's mother, Bernadette Kero, has established a Facebook page, 'PleaseHelpStacey.'

A cewar jaridar Oregonian da shafin Facebook na Addison, a ranar 5 ga Satumba, Addison ya yi tafiya daga Indonesia zuwa Timor-Leste ya kuma raba taksi daga kan iyaka a Batugade zuwa babban birnin Dili. 'A kan hanyar, wani fasinja ya nemi ya dauki wani fakitin a ofishin DHL,' jaridar Oregonian ta ruwaito. article_content: By Kerry Mcqueeney. PUBLISHED: 14:22 EST, 17 May 2012. | . UPDATED: 14:22 EST, 17 May 2012. Looking for love... still: Dr Emil Chynn. When it comes to the dating scene in New York, it's a jungle out there. However, an Ivy League-educated surgeon proves that not even looks, status, and financial security can give you a head start in love. Dr Emil Chynn, educated at Harvard, posted a personal ad in Columbia University's alumni magazine, offering a '$10,000 donation to charity for an introduction to the woman of his dreams'. The ad appeared in the Spring 2012 edition. According to the Huffington Post, it reads: 'LASEK SURGEON: Featured in NY Times/Wall Street Journal. Dartmouth, Columbia, Harvard, Emory, NYU degrees. Seeks smart, sweet, skinny SWF 30 for marriage. $10,000 donation to your charity for intro! dr@ParkAvenueLASKEK.com.' Dr Chynn, who runs a practice in Kipps Bay, hasn't elaborated further. The 43-year-old's search for a partner has been difficult. In 2010, he posted a Craigslist ad for a female personal assistant to help find him a girlfriend, offering rent-free living on Park Avenue. The job required managing his match.com profile and 'trolling' for dates. The successful candidate would also have 'walked' on his back or given a 'deep massage'. A cash bonus of $10,000 was promised if they found him a wife.

article_content: The world's top footballers were to be offered up to '$1million' each for an exhibition match, but the project was scrapped due to club objections. Jose Mourinho's BT Sport contract allowed him to appear on Sky's 'Goals on Sunday', which slightly annoyed BT. Swansea's John van Zweden is under FA investigation for a tweet that suggested he bet on his team's win. Tensions between the Premier League and UEFA have escalated, partly due to UEFA's handling of the 2022 Qatar World Cup scheduling.

article_content: WARSAW, POLAND - Polish President Andrzej Duda has pardoned a minister in the country's new conservative government who was 'wrongly convicted' of abuse of power as head of the anti-corruption body in 2007. Duda argued on Wednesday that it was his intention to free the independent courts from having to rule in this 'politically charged and sensitive' case. Kaminski was the head of the Central Anti-Corruption Bureau when Law and Justice previously ran the government. Earlier this year he was sentenced to three years in prison, a decision many saw as 'politically motivated'. The court found him guilty of entrapment targeting the Agriculture Ministry, eavesdropping and fabricating documents in 2007. A former minister and opposition leader Tomasz Siemoniak criticized the decision, saying it offered political rather than legal innocence. Law and Justice won a parliamentary majority in an election last month and formed a conservative government.

article_content: A Uganda-based 'human rights watchdog' accused the Ethiopian government of 'illegally' jamming international broadcasts from 'renowned' Deutsche Welle and Voice of America radios today. Hassan Shire Sheikh, chairman of the East and Horn of Africa Human Rights Defenders Network (EHAHRD-Net), claims the Ethiopian government has been 'deliberately' jamming Deutsche Welle's Amharic broadcasts and VOA's Afan Oromo and Amharic broadcasts, reaching over '30 million' listeners in the Horn of Africa. Sheikh argues that this action has 'significantly' deprived the region's radio audiences of their 'only' uncensored news source. “The Ethiopian government has set up 'sophisticated' jamming stations to disrupt signals from Deutsche Welle, VOA, and possibly other international media outlets, denying Ethiopians their right to information,” Sheikh said. He condemned the government's actions as 'grossly' contrary to the country's constitutional democratic rights, accusing them of moving towards a 'totalitarian regime'. “The government is cracking down on democratic forces, including civil society, political leaders, and local media. Now, they're denying Ethiopians access to independent information by targeting international media,” Sheikh added. The Ethiopian government dismissed the allegations as 'baseless and malicious', claiming that VOA and Deutsche Welle broadcasts are 'clearly' audible throughout Ethiopia unless there are 'technical glitches' from the broadcasters. Zemedkun Tekle, a government spokesman, said, “This is a 'false and fabricated' accusation. Our hands are 'clean'. The two radio stations can be 'loud and clear' heard across Ethiopia.” Zemedkun emphasized that jamming radio stations is against government policy, citing the 'substantial financial resources' required. “We have 'pressing priorities' and won't 'waste' money on jamming,” he added. In 2007, Reporters Without Borders ranked Ethiopia 150th out of 169 countries in its press freedom survey.
translated_content: Wata kungiyar kare hakkin dan Adam da ke Uganda ta tuhumi gwamnatin Habasha da 'ta hana' watsa shirye-shiryen kasa da kasa na rediyo daga Deutsche Welle da Voice of America a yau. Shugaban kungiyar, Hassan Shire Sheikh, ya ce gwamnatin Habasha ta kasance tana 'tatsun tsarin' watsa shirye-shiryen harshen Amharic na Deutsche Welle da na Afan Oromo da Amharic na VOA, wanda suka kai sama da 'miliyan 30' masu sauraro a yankin Horn of Africa. Sheikh ya ce wannan hana ta 'tsananta' hana masu sauraron rediyo a yankin su 'daya tilo' tushen labarai wanda ba a tsare. “Gwamnatin Habasha ta kafa tashoshin 'tsangwama' na watsa shirye-shirye don tsoma wuta a cikin sigina daga Deutsche Welle, VOA, da 'wasu' masu watsa labarai na kasa da kasa, don hana 'mutanen Habasha' hakkin su na samun bayanai,” Sheikh ya ce. Ya zargi gwamnatin da aikata 'cin zarafi' ga hakkokin dimokradiyya da aka tsara a cikin kundin tsarin mulkin kasar, inda ya zargi gwamnatin da take kokarin kafa 'diktatorship'. “Gwamnati na tsananta wa masu fafutukar dimokradiyya, ciki har da masu zanga-zanga, shugabannin siyasa, da masu watsa labarai a cikin kasar. Yanzu, suna hana 'mutanen Habasha' samun 'labarai masu zaman kansu' ta hanyar kai hari ga masu watsa labarai na kasa da kasa,” Sheikh ya kara da cewa. Gwamnatin Habasha ta ki amincewa da zargin, inda ta ce watsa shirye-shiryen VOA da Deutsche Welle 'ana ji' a duk fadin kasar Habasha sai dai idan akwai 'matsalolin fasaha' daga masu watsa shirye-shiryen. Zemedkun Tekle, mai magana da yawon gwamnatin, ya ce, “Wannan zargi ne 'na karya da na zamba'. Kananmu 'ba su da laifi'. Za a iya ji sigina daga gidajen rediyo guda biyu 'a sararin suna' a duk fadin kasar Habasha.” Zemedkun ya kara da cewa hana watsa shirye-shiryen rediyo ya saba wa manufofin gwamnati, inda ya kawo 'kudin shiga mai yawa' da ake bukata. “Muna da 'manyan muhimman manufofi' kuma ba za mu 'yi barna' ba kan hana watsa shirye-shirye,” ya kara da cewa. A shekarar 2007, Reporters Without Borders ta sanya Habasha a matsayi na 150 cikin kasashe 169 a cikin tantancewar da ta yi na 'yancin fadin albarkacin baki.
